extracted.intended_audience: EPA rulemakers, environmental attorneys, policy analysts, and stakeholders submitting or evaluating notice-and-comment rulemaking on CAA §112 MACT/residual risk
extracted.subtask_description: Detailed public-comment guidance and legal critique directed at EPA's proposed MACT and residual-risk rule for oil & gas source categories, focusing on statutory duties under CAA §§112(d) and 112(f). Advises what analyses, data, and legal considerations EPA must include in final rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ample margin of safety determination must consider full range of control options
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA’s ample margin determination relies almost exclusively on cost-effectiveness of very limited control options and fails to consider the full range of control options available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA must explain what searches it conducted for control options and why other options were rejected. It should consider options such as desiccant dehydrators, control options demonstrated by the Natural Gas Star program, technologies/practices from BACT determinations (including greater control efficiency levels), practices used in EPA refinery enforcement (e.g., more stringent LDAR), vendor literature and vendor discussions on newer technologies, state requirements/programs (California, Colorado, Wyoming), and options summarized in the Paranhos summary and Buckheit and Sahu Reports. Failure to consider the full range renders the analysis cursory, arbitrary, and capricious.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide reasoned explanation for limiting analyzed control options
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA nowhere explains why it limited its analysis under the §112(f) ample-margin analysis to only a few selected options or why other options were rejected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The agency must document what other options it considered, what searches it conducted, and provide reasoned explanations for rejections. Absent such explanation, the determination is arbitrary and capricious.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support assumptions about cost-effectiveness scaling between small and large units
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA assumed, without basis, that the cost effectiveness for large dehydrators would not exceed twice that of small units.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA must support or justify scaling assumptions (e.g., by cost models or data). Typical scaling suggests cost-effectiveness of larger units is smaller (due to economies of scale); EPA must explain departures from that expectation with evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support assumptions about control device efficiency (e.g., 95% vs higher)
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA assumed control devices (condenser or combustion device) achieve at least a 95% HAP reduction but did not explain why 95% (and not 98% or 99%) was used or analyze impacts of higher efficiencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA must investigate the cost-effectiveness impact of greater control efficiencies and justify the chosen efficiency assumptions with empirical data or vendor/manufacturer information and test data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support assumptions that costs of second control device equal first device
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA assumed costs for adding a second control device equal the costs of the first device without justification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because control-device cost depends on process size, flow rate, contaminant concentration, etc., EPA must explain or substantiate this cost-equality assumption (or use size-specific cost estimates).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide basis for HAP fraction of VOC assumption in LDAR cost-effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA asserted that HAP present is approximately 1/20 the VOC present (i.e., 5%) for LDAR cost-effectiveness comparisons but provided no clear data basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA must supply the data or rationale supporting the HAP:VOC fraction used, or otherwise reassess LDAR cost-effectiveness with defensible HAP composition data given poor HAP data support in fugitive source inventories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduce benzene limit for glycol dehydrator area sources if alternative removed for majors
rubrics_metrics.description: Currently EPA retains a benzene limit of 0.9 Mg for glycol dehydrator area sources—the same as the alternative compliance option for major sources—but recognizes removal for majors would significantly reduce public health risk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA cannot lawfully or reasonably retain the same alternative compliance option for area sources if it removes it for major sources; keeping it would be arbitrary and capricious. EPA must reduce the benzene limit for area sources accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: May not pre-decide to skip statutorily required 8-year residual risk review
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA stated it did not believe another residual risk review under §112(f) would be necessary for the two source categories 8 years following promulgation due to the addition of new MACT requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 112(f)(2) imposes a mandatory duty to review and, if required, set a residual risk standard eight years after promulgation; EPA may not lawfully decide now not to perform that review. The decision must be based on factual circumstances at the future time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider environmental/ecological risks separately and perform ecological assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA treated ecological risk as generally protected where human health is protected and provided only cursory multipathway/ecological discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA must perform an ecological risk assessment rather than rely solely on human-health assessment and must not assume human-protection implies ecological-protection. It must address data indicating potential adverse impacts on plants, birds, or other wildlife, and carry out Endangered Species Act consultation where required. The SAB warned that assuming ecological receptors are protected if humans are is incorrect; persistent or bioaccumulative chemicals require special consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use current, reliable, representative emission test data in §112(d) review
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA apparently did not use or analyze any current emission test data in its §112(d) proposal, raising questions about how it satisfied §112(d)(6) duties to assess developments since 1999.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA must use current, representative emission-test data to assess industry practices/processes/technologies. If existing inventories (e.g., 2005 NEI) are insufficient or unrepresentative, EPA must collect the emission test data needed to recalculate MACT floors for glycol dehydrators, storage vessels, and equipment leaks.

rubrics_metrics.name: §112(d)(6) review must take into account developments in practices, processes, and control technologies
rubrics_metrics.description: At least every eight years, EPA is required to review and revise as necessary the technology-based standards, taking into account developments in practices, processes, and control technologies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When revising under §112(d)(6), EPA must apply the substantive requirements of §112(d)(2)-(3) (i.e., MACT floor and beyond-the-floor analyses), treating §112(d)(6) as an ongoing ratchet that updates standards to reflect what is achievable in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recalculate MACT floor when post-original developments show lower achievable emissions
rubrics_metrics.description: There is evidence that sources have achieved levels of actual HAP emissions below the existing MACT and EPA's proposed standard; §112(d)(6) requires EPA to revise MACT if necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA must recalculate MACT floors based on current data (including post-original data) where developments in technology/practice demonstrate greater reductions achieved in practice, consistent with D.C. Circuit precedent (e.g., HMIWI). The agency may not confine itself to the data set used when floors were originally set if that set is unsupportive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set numeric limits for each HAP emitted rather than only percent-reduction requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA's approach of requiring a 95% reduction across-the-board (rather than numeric limits for each HAP) may fail to satisfy the MACT requirement to set standards based on emission levels achieved in practice for each HAP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 112(d)(3) and (6) require EPA to consider numeric emission limits for each HAP and to close gaps in the original MACT by setting standards for uncontrolled HAPs. EPA must calculate the MACT floor on a per-HAP basis where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct beyond-the-floor analysis only after proper MACT floor recalculation
rubrics_metrics.description: Absent an up-to-date MACT floor determination based on current emission controls and data, a beyond-the-floor determination cannot be meaningful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA must first recalculate and set accurate MACT floors; then it must conduct a beyond-the-floor analysis in accordance with §112(d)(2), taking into account cost and other statutory factors when considering beyond-the-floor stringency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider emissions from control devices themselves
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA overlooks potential HAP emissions that control devices themselves may emit and has not collected such emissions data from facilities with installed control devices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA must include emissions from control devices in its inventory/assessment and collect such data where lacking, because failure to do so may bias MACT and residual risk analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt lower LDAR thresholds and best-performing practices across equipment
rubrics_metrics.description: Commenters support lowering LDAR threshold for valves from 10,000 to 500 ppm but note EPA's proposal does not extend lower thresholds to other equipment or adopt LDAR practices used by best-performing sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA should align §112(d) requirements with NSPS proposals (lower thresholds across equipment) and adopt LDAR practices employed by best-performing sources in the category rather than limiting to a subset of equipment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid reliance on incomplete or outdated datasets and demonstrate representativeness
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA relies on incomplete and outdated datasets (e.g., 1997 survey, possibly 2005 NEI) that may not represent current sector emissions or performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA must demonstrate that datasets used are representative for MACT-floor purposes; if not, it must collect new emission data. Even where 2005 NEI covers more sources than 1997, EPA must assess its reliability and representativeness before using it to set floors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Look back and look around in 8-year review; interpret 'developments' expansively
rubrics_metrics.description: §112(d)(6) requires EPA to 'look back' to fix prior defects and 'look around' to capture developments; EPA interprets 'developments' too narrowly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA must cast a wide net in evaluating control options (including practices, processes, and technologies), consult vendor literature and vendors, examine state programs, consider enforcement/practices used elsewhere, and incorporate outside technical reports (Buckheit, Sahu, Paranhos) rather than narrowly limiting its review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct flaws in original MACT derivation and update standards accordingly
rubrics_metrics.description: The original 1999 MACT derivation for glycol dehydrators relied on flawed surveys and judgment calls (e.g., assuming 95% reduction without using observed up-to-99% control efficiencies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA must resolve information gaps, recalculate the MACT floor for each HAP emitted by large glycol dehydrators, and set standards that reflect the emission levels of the most efficient performers as required by §112(d). Court precedent has rejected practices such as requiring MACT be achievable by all sources or setting 'no control' MACT floors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider setting beyond-the-floor standards accounting for statutory factors
rubrics_metrics.description: After establishing updated floors, §112(d)(2) requires EPA to consider whether more stringent beyond-the-floor standards are achievable, taking into account factors including cost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA must perform a proper beyond-the-floor analysis (after recalculating floors) and may consider costs and other statutory factors when deciding beyond-the-floor stringency; it must not use cost to evade recalculation of floors where developments warrant stricter floors.
